category_title: Underachieving students in difficult PE contexts who alternate between task involvement and ephemeral off-task behaviors
minimal_context: Students are working in small groups practicing somersaults on mats during a gymnastics workshop in PE class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please get into your groups of three to five and practice performing somersaults on the mats.

STUDENT: (Exercises briefly, then suddenly leaves the task to go talk to another student in a nearby group) If the teacher wasn't there, we'd just have fun all day.

TUTOR: Let's get back to your own mat and keep practicing.

STUDENT: (Regularly checks the teacher's location in the classroom to be discreet) It's cool; we're winding each other up with my mates, making jokes (laughs).

TUTOR: Make sure you are taking turns doing the somersaults.

STUDENT: (Pushes another student during a somersault to make them fall) Yeah, here I'm having a bit of fun with my mate ...(laughs), he's going for a roll and boom ...I push him. He fell over ...We have a laugh together, he did it to me earlier ...We're just having fun ...

options.A: Observe their reactions—especially their facial expressions, the nature of their laughs, and signs of becoming upset—and intervene firmly when detecting the beginning of a violent conflict.
options.B: Transition the student to structured constructive play, providing simple instruction cards and easy-to-succeed tasks for the remainder of the gymnastics workshop.
options.C: Move to the mat, physically guide the student into a starting position for the somersault, kneel by their feet, and grab their hands for the activity.
options.D: Guide the student through a 'bubble-blowing' visualization technique to help them visualize their thoughts and release them without judgment during the gymnastics activity.
